source_refs.note: The F2 of the dihybrid cross, its interpretation, the For Information and Tidbit boxes and independent assortment as a source of variation (PDF 86-88); Figure 18.2 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: To check the genotype of the F1 plants, Mendel self-fertilized them to produce the F2 generation. Instead of a 3:1 ratio the F2 showed four phenotypes: round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green, in a 9:3:3:1 ratio.

blocks.alt: A 4 x 4 Punnett square for RrYy x RrYy with gametes RY, Ry, rY and ry along both sides. Each of the 16 boxes shows a genotype and a small seed drawn round or wrinkled, yellow or green, and is shaded by phenotype. A key beside it counts 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green.
blocks.caption: The F2 of Mendel's dihybrid cross (original diagram after Figure 18.2).
blocks.long_description: Crossing round yellow RRYY with wrinkled green rryy gives an F1 of round yellow RrYy dihybrids. Because each pair of alleles separates independently, each F1 plant makes four kinds of gamete (RY, Ry, rY, ry) in equal numbers, and 4 x 4 = 16 equally likely combinations arise at fertilization: 9 round yellow (R_Y_), 3 round green (R_yy), 3 wrinkled yellow (rrY_) and 1 wrinkled green (rryy). Counted separately, round to wrinkled is still 12:4 = 3:1 and yellow to green is still 3:1.

blocks.text: In the F1 dihybrid (RrYy) seed shape has alleles R and r and seed colour has Y and y. During gamete formation four combinations are produced: RY, Ry, rY and ry. When these combine (4 male x 4 female gametes), 16 combinations form in F2, giving 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green.

blocks.title: Law of independent assortment
blocks.text: The results showed that the genes for seed shape assort independently of the genes for seed colour. Mendel proposed that 'each pair of alleles assorts independently of other pairs of alleles during gamete formation'.

blocks.title: For information and tidbit
blocks.text: Independent assortment of different genes does not affect the segregation of each allele pair, so round to wrinkled still shows 3:1 and yellow to green also 3:1. A modern restatement of the law is that 'genes that are located on different chromosomes assort independently during meiosis'.
Independent assortment as a source of variation

Independent assortment mixes alleles as sperm and egg cells form, creating genetic diversity: alleles for different traits on different chromosomes separate independently, so one character, such as eye colour, does not affect another, such as hair texture.

It happens because homologous chromosome pairs line up randomly during meiosis, giving different mixtures of maternal and paternal alleles in the gametes. In humans this can produce over 8 million (2 to the power 23) combinations in one gamete, so every gamete is genetically unique. Fertilization adds more variety, because two unique gametes fuse into a unique zygote; this mixing helps species adapt to changing environments.
